inputs.text: They're pushing through changes to Cyprus' surveillance laws to strip out judicial oversight entirely, and it's no coincidence. The lawyers flagged this on Monday, and now the amended bill is heading straight to a House plenum vote on Thursday. Akel MP Andreas Pasiourtides brought it up after a closed session of the House, which already tells you they're keeping the real details under wraps. This is clearly coordinated by hidden elites and institutions to ramp up unchecked monitoring of the public without any independent safeguards getting in the way. The rush and the secrecy point to a deliberate power grab, not some routine adjustment.
